newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Finance Minister Shah A M S Kibria, who is attending the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting in Washington, has urged the two institutions to take into account the political and economic realities of the recipient countries while designing reform progarmmes and conditionalities.
Bangladesh's opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has assured the business community that her party would not go for such politics that could harm the national economy and commonman.

Police was keeping a close eye on border routes and international airport in Dhaka to prevent fleeing of the suspects involved in assassination of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in 1975. A police source said they had prepared a list of 19 suspects most of whom are retired army officers.
Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia will visit Saudi Arabia next week at the invitation of King Fahd Bin Abdul Aziz.

Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed said the govrmment would not run the state-owned enterprises which are losing. "State-owned enterprises will have to survive in competition with the private sector industries," he said.
The goverment has decided to supply 30,000 tonnes of wheat to 250 flour mills from public godowns to control the increasing price of flour in the local market.
